data.current_description: The free tool behind the homepage scanner and /ip-lookup. Same verdict pipeline as /v1/lookup but unauthenticated and rate-limited to 12/minute and 80/day per caller IP (an IPv6 caller's whole /64 shares 72/minute and 480/day). Pasted forms such as 1.2.3.4:80, [2001:db8::1]:443, a URL, fullwidth digits or ::ffff:1.2.3.4 are read as the address they name, and an IPv6 address is answered in its RFC 5952 form. Invalid input does not count toward those limits (it has its own, 60/minute). For production traffic use /v1/lookup with an API key.

data.current_summary: Free bulk IP check (no email required)
data.current_description: Check up to 20 unique public IPs in one call. Does not collect email, subscribe callers or send mail; an email supplied by a legacy client is ignored. Limited to 3 batches/hour per caller IP (an IPv6 /64 shares 12 batches/hour); a batch with no valid public address does not count. Entries are read like /api/lookup and deduplicated after that. IP-only results do not establish that a visitor is safe or provide browser evidence. For sustained bulk use, call /v1/lookup with an API key.

data.current_summary: Exchange an API key for a short-lived bearer token
data.current_description: OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant. client_id is your account email and client_secret is your current live or personal test API key; a previous live key in its rotation grace period cannot mint tokens. The access_token carries the account id and key type, never the API key. It expires after 3600 seconds. It is bound to the key it was minted with and authenticates as the account's current key of that type while that key still works: after a rotation, a token minted from the previous live key keeps working through that key's 24-hour grace; revoking the previous key, a second rotation, or rotating the test key ends such tokens at once (401), so mint a new token on a 401. Use Bearer authentication on /v1/*; authenticated MCP also accepts tokens minted with live keys. Supply exchange credentials in the form body (client_secret_post) or through HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic). Token responses send no-store. A live key's IP allowlist applies to minting too (since 2026-09-28): from an address outside the list the answer is 400 unauthorized_client and no token; the test key is exempt. Limited to 60 exchanges/minute/IP; a 429 carries Retry-After: 60. Discovery: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
data.description_suggestion: Exchange account credentials for a short-lived OAuth 2.0 bearer token using the client_credentials grant. Credentials: client_id (account email) and client_secret (current live or personal test API key). Returns access_token valid for 3600 seconds, bound to the key used for minting. Token authenticates as the account's current key of that type; after key rotation, tokens from the previous key remain valid through its 24-hour grace period. Tokens are invalidated immediately if the previous key is revoked, a second rotation occurs, or the test key is rotated. Use returned token with Bearer authentication on /v1/* endpoints. Supply credentials via form body (client_secret_post) or HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic). Rate-limited to 60 exchanges/minute/IP. IP allowlist on live keys applies to token minting; test keys are exempt. See /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server for discovery.

data.current_summary: Look up an arbitrary IP address
data.current_description: Returns an allow/review/block verdict and 0-100 risk score for a public IP. A bare lookup checks two things: Tor exit lists (tor, block at 90) and published cloud-server ranges (dch, review at 40). When the public routing table knows the address, `network` also carries its ASN, AS name and AS registration country with `source: "asn_table"`; that label is for display only and never changes the verdict or score. `country` and `city` stay null on a bare lookup (the registration country is where the network is registered, not where a visitor is). known:false means neither list matched, not that the IP is safe. VPN and proxy verdicts need a live visit: use POST /v1/evaluate with the browser SDK evidence. Shares the account's hourly quota with /v1/evaluate.
data.description_suggestion: Returns a fraud verdict (allow/review/block) and 0-100 risk score for a public IP address. A bare lookup checks Tor exit lists and published cloud-server ranges. When available, the response includes network ASN, AS name, and registration country from the public routing table (for display only; does not affect verdict or score). Geographic fields (country, city) are null for bare lookups. Note: known:false indicates no match in threat lists, not safety confirmation. data.current_description: Forward the client-side Maskbreak token for full network intelligence. With an account key or OAuth token, a missing, null or empty client token is accepted as a degraded HTTP fallback: the visitor's address is then unknown (ip: "unknown"), so the network layer, the Tor exit list and the cloud ranges cannot run, and the answer is allow with degraded: true unless device, email or policy signals say otherwise. Without a retrievable device event the decision comes from the network layer alone; device is omitted and degraded is not set. The public sandbox requires a deterministic test token. Official server SDKs currently require a non-empty token. Send the body as application/json; since 28 September 2026 a JSON object sent as text/plain, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, application/*+json or without a Content-Type is read the same way (before, such a body was ignored and the call answered as if no token had been sent), and a form body sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded (token=…&fingerprintEventId=…&email=…&tz=…) gives those string fields. A multipart body is not read. The Bearer scheme name is case-insensitive. The response carries both legacy fields (status / isSuspicious / details / deviceIntel) and modern fields (decision / risk_score / network / device / reasons).
data.summary_suggestion: Score a visitor session for fraud signals
data.description_suggestion: Evaluates a visitor session for fraud, VPN, proxy, bot, and antidetect-browser signals using network and device intelligence. Submit the client-side Maskbreak token (from the browser SDK) along with optional fingerprintEventId, email, and timezone for full analysis. Returns a fraud decision (allow/review/block), 0-100 risk score, and detailed signal breakdown (network, device, reasons). Degraded mode: if the token is missing, null, or empty, the evaluation proceeds with network signals only (ip: "unknown"), returning allow with degraded: true unless device or policy signals override. Device signals are omitted without a retrievable device event. Accepts application/json, text/plain, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, or form-encoded bodies. Consumes one evaluation from your monthly quota.

data.current_description: The free tool behind the homepage scanner and /ip-lookup. Same verdict pipeline as /v1/lookup but unauthenticated and rate-limited to 12/minute and 80/day per caller IP (an IPv6 caller's whole /64 shares 72/minute and 480/day). Pasted forms such as 1.2.3.4:80, [2001:db8::1]:443, a URL, fullwidth digits or ::ffff:1.2.3.4 are read as the address they name, and an IPv6 address is answered in its RFC 5952 form. Invalid input does not count toward those limits (it has its own, 60/minute). For production traffic use /v1/lookup with an API key.
data.description_suggestion: Unauthenticated IP reputation lookup using the same verdict pipeline as /v1/lookup. data.current_summary: Exchange an API key for a short-lived bearer token
data.current_description: OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant. client_id is your account email and client_secret is your current live or personal test API key; a previous live key in its rotation grace period cannot mint tokens. The access_token carries the account id and key type, never the API key. It expires after 3600 seconds. It is bound to the key it was minted with and authenticates as the account's current key of that type while that key still works: after a rotation, a token minted from the previous live key keeps working through that key's 24-hour grace; revoking the previous key, a second rotation, or rotating the test key ends such tokens at once (401), so mint a new token on a 401. Use Bearer authentication on /v1/*; authenticated MCP also accepts tokens minted with live keys. Supply exchange credentials in the form body (client_secret_post) or through HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic). Token responses send no-store. A live key's IP allowlist applies to minting too (since 2026-09-28): from an address outside the list the answer is 400 unauthorized_client and no token; the test key is exempt. Limited to 60 exchanges/minute/IP; a 429 carries Retry-After: 60. Discovery: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
data.description_suggestion: Exchange account credentials for a short-lived OAuth 2.0 bearer token using the client_credentials grant. Provide client_id (account email) and client_secret (current live or personal test API key) via form body (client_secret_post) or HTTP Basic authentication (client_secret_basic). Returns an access_token valid for 3600 seconds, bound to the key it was minted from. Token authenticates as the account's current key of that type and can be used with Bearer authentication on /v1/* endpoints and authenticated MCP. Token lifecycle: tokens remain valid through a key's 24-hour rotation grace period but become invalid (401) if the key is revoked, rotated a second time, or the test key is rotated. IP allowlist restrictions on live keys apply to token minting (test key exempt). Rate-limited to 60 exchanges/minute per IP; 429 responses include Retry-After: 60. OAuth discovery available at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

data.current_summary: Look up an arbitrary IP address
data.current_description: Returns an allow/review/block verdict and 0-100 risk score for a public IP. A bare lookup checks two things: Tor exit lists (tor, block at 90) and published cloud-server ranges (dch, review at 40). When the public routing table knows the address, `network` also carries its ASN, AS name and AS registration country with `source: "asn_table"`; that label is for display only and never changes the verdict or score. `country` and `city` stay null on a bare lookup (the registration country is where the network is registered, not where a visitor is). known:false means neither list matched, not that the IP is safe. VPN and proxy verdicts need a live visit: use POST /v1/evaluate with the browser SDK evidence. Shares the account's hourly quota with /v1/evaluate.

data.current_description: Forward the client-side Maskbreak token for full network intelligence. With an account key or OAuth token, a missing, null or empty client token is accepted as a degraded HTTP fallback: the visitor's address is then unknown (ip: "unknown"), so the network layer, the Tor exit list and the cloud ranges cannot run, and the answer is allow with degraded: true unless device, email or policy signals say otherwise. Without a retrievable device event the decision comes from the network layer alone; device is omitted and degraded is not set. The public sandbox requires a deterministic test token. Official server SDKs currently require a non-empty token. Send the body as application/json; since 28 September 2026 a JSON object sent as text/plain, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, application/*+json or without a Content-Type is read the same way (before, such a body was ignored and the call answered as if no token had been sent), and a form body sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded (token=…&fingerprintEventId=…&email=…&tz=…) gives those string fields. A multipart body is not read. The Bearer scheme name is case-insensitive. The response carries both legacy fields (status / isSuspicious / details / deviceIntel) and modern fields (decision / risk_score / network / device / reasons).

Response includes both legacy fields (status, isSuspicious, details, deviceIntel) and modern fields (decision, risk_score, network, device, reasons). Consumes 1 visitor check from your monthly quota. Supports application/json and application/x-www-form-urlencoded request bodies.
